== ==
 RAUSHAN KUMAR Son of Nand Kishore Prasad Resident of Mohalla-121,
 Naya Tola, P.O. and P.S.-Patna City Chowk, Patan Devi, District-Patna.

... ... P  Versus  1. The State of Bihar  2. RAKHI KUMARI Wife of Raushan Kumar, D/o Kailash Prasad Resident of  Mohalla-Postal Park, Road No. 3/B, P.S.-Jakkanpur, District-Patna.
 ... ...

Opposite Party/s  ======================================================
 Appearance :
 For the Petitioner/s : Mr.Rajeev Kumar  For the Opposite Party/s : Mr.Shailendra Kumar  ======================================================
 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE SATYAVRAT VERMA  ORAL ORDER 3 16-05-2024

1. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned A.P.P. for the State.
2. The petitioner apprehends his arrest in a case registered for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
3. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that office report dated 26-4-2024 records that ordinary notice has been received by the OP No. 2 personally but receipt for the same was recorded by her brother as reported by the process server.
4.
In view of the report of the process server, the notice is deemed to have been validly served.
Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.15836 of 2024(3) dt.16-05-2024 5.
The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner, being husband, has been falsely implicated in the instant case by the complainant.
It is next submitted that the complainant, despite receiving notice, chooses not to appear and contest.
It is also submitted that the petitioner is always willing to keep the complainant with honor and dignity.

It is next submitted that no useful purpose Raushan Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178492782/
1 would be served by sending the petitioner to jail as petitioner is willing to pay a monthly maintenance of Rs. 3,000/- to the complainant.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also submitted that with passage of time and on intervention of well- wishers, the parties may come on amicable terms.
It is further submitted that the maintenance would commence from 1-6- 2024.

6. Considering the submission made by the learned counsel for the petitioner, the petitioner above-named, in the event of his arrest or surrender before the learned Court below within a period of six weeks from today, be released on anticipatory bail on furnishing bail bonds of Rs. 5,000/-
(Rupees Five Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned court below where the case is pending/successor court in connection with Complaint Case No.
6465(C) of 2021, subject to the conditions as laid down under Patna High Court CR. MISC.
No.15836 of 2024(3) dt.16-05-2024 Section 438 (2) of the Cr.P.C.
7.

However, it is made clear that OP No. 2 shall be at liberty to file an application before this court seeking cancellation of the anticipatory bail granted to the petitioner, in the event if the petitioner does not give the monthly maintenance as agreed for two consecutive months.

(Satyavrat Verma, J) SUMIT/-
